title: Cap. VII: Placeus denies the confession — force of one sin versus numerical ingress
pass_a_gloss: Placeus turns to the candid reader: what if the author of the fourth argument never made the confession Garissoles attributes to him? He does not acknowledge, hold, or state—either in identical wording or in equivalents—that the entering sin is Adam's one sin in the charged sense. All he said was that one man's one sin carried force enough to doom the whole human multitude. He never said that numerically identical act walked into every person and immediately dragged death with it. What entered the world is the effect of that one sin; sin and death came through one man by the power of that sin as it spread, multiplied, and traveled with the human nature to which it clings. Condemnation of the multitude follows from that propagation into all and from multiplication by headcount. That reading is the excellent man's mind and contradicts neither himself nor Placeus.
pass_b_english: But what will you say, candid reader, if the most learned author of that reason does not confess what he is here said to confess? Certainly he does not acknowledge that that sin which is said to have entered through one man is one sin of one man, namely Adam's: he does not hold that; he said it neither in so many words nor in equivalent ones. He said only that in one man's one sin there was such force that it should sentence the whole multitude of men to death; but he did not say that that one sin of one man entered into all men as the same in number, and brought death in immediately. Namely, the sin that entered into the world is the effect of one sin of one man; and through one man sin entered into the world, and death by the force of one sin, which diffused and multiplied itself by natural propagation, and propagated with the human nature in which it inheres. Therefore it sentenced the whole multitude of men to death by its propagation into all men, and by multiplication according to number. This is that most excellent man's mind, contradicting neither himself nor Placeus.
source_text: Quid vero dices, candide Lector, si id non confitetur doctissimus autor illius rationis, quod hic confiteri dicitur? Certe non agnoscit peccatum illud, quod per unum hominem introiisse dicitur, esse unum unius hominis, nempe Adami peccatum: id non sentit: id neque totidem verbis dixit, neque aequipollentibus. Dixit tantum in uno unius peccato tantam fuisse vim, ut totam hominum multitudinem morti addiceret: sed non dixit illud unum unius peccatum idem numero in omnes homines ingressum esse, & proxime mortem invexisse. Nempe peccatum quod introiit in mundum est unius peccati unius hominis effectum, & per unum hominem peccatum introiit in mundum & mors vi unius peccati, quod sese propagatione naturali diffudit, & multiplicavit, & cum natura humana, cui inhaeret, propagavit. Itaque totam hominum multitudinem morti addixit sui in omnes homines propagatione, ac secundum numerum multiplicatione. Haec est praestantissimi illius viri mens, neque sibi, neque Placeo contradicentis.
